design.affected_system: housing-stability, eviction prevention, shelter diversion, and support coordination
alternatives: verify the highest-consequence signals before acting on housing-instability pathways and prevention-service gaps
combine targeted inspection, monitoring, and data-quality repair for housing-instability pathways and prevention-service gaps
pair privacy-preserving longitudinal pathway diagnosis with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Court, assistance, shelter, outreach, housing, and service records use privacy-preserving linkage.
Risk models support outreach only and never determine legal rights or automatic denial.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue current inspection and reporting practice for housing-instability pathways and prevention-service gaps.

constraints.description: The homelessness prevention and housing stability diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: homelessness response director and housing-stability administrator
design.decision_question: Where do rent burden, court filings, shelter entry, benefit loss, and service access reveal preventable system gaps?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The homelessness prevention and housing stability diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for housing-instability pathways and prevention-service gaps passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.
independence_key.primary_outcome: eligible households entering crisis without prior prevention access

design.intended_claim: A versioned diagnose design for comparing declared alternatives affecting housing-instability pathways and prevention-service gaps, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: eligible households entering crisis without prior prevention access
distributional gap in eligible households entering crisis without prior prevention access
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not label a household homeless, likely to be evicted, or noncompliant from proxy variables.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for housing-instability pathways and prevention-service gaps passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

design.title: Diagnose housing-instability and prevention-service gaps
transportability_risks: Eviction law, rents, benefits, shelter systems, informal displacement, and data linkage differ.
Administrative records omit people who do not seek or cannot access services.

family.affected_system: housing-stability, eviction prevention, shelter diversion, and support coordination
claim_boundary: Requests, listings, parcels, and administrative records do not alone verify conditions or need.
Screened sites and portfolios are not permits, acquisitions, adopted plans, or completed housing.
Displacement, affordability, habitability, and program effects require direct outcomes and identification.
family.decision_owner: homelessness response director and housing-stability administrator
family.description: Eight decisions for instability diagnosis, service-demand forecasting, prevention portfolios, access siting, assistance allocation, case scheduling, surge stress, and program evaluation.
family.title: Homelessness prevention and housing stability

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
